examples.explanation: 孟子才三岁开始搬家 → 孟子才三岁就开始搬家: at only age three, the action already starts, so use 才 Num.就V.

examples.display: [会→就]生病了
examples.her_note: 会means “will”, for future
examples.explanation: 会生病了 → 就生病了: this is the result of the condition, so use 就; 会 means “will” for the future.

card.not_an_error: When you mean “sometimes,” use 有的时候, not 只要……就. 会 is appropriate when you mean “will” in the future.

name: 不是……而是……
definition: 不是……而是…… refutes something conventional or mistaken and affirms an unexpected correction. Use it only when the two alternatives have that correction relationship.
her_notes: “不是……而是……” is used to refute something conventional and affirm something unexpected, and to correct something wrong
“不是……而是……” is used to refute something conventional and affirm something unexpected, and to correct something wrong, 搬家is not conventionally related to看文章
“不是……而是……” is used to refute something conventional and affirm something unexpected, and to correct something wrong, 画画儿 is not a conventional activity related to 寺庙

card.rule: Use 不是……而是…… only to correct a conventional or mistaken idea with an unexpected alternative. Put the subject before 不是……而是…… when both alternatives have the same subject.
card.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: 不是……而是…… must refute a mistaken or expected idea and give its correction; <first alternative> is not conventionally related to <second alternative>.

examples.display: ⟦不是商店而是学校⟧
examples.her_note: “不是……而是……” is used to refute something conventional and affirm something unexpected, and to correct something wrong, 商店is not conventionally related to对教育有好处
examples.explanation: 不是商店而是学校: 商店 is not conventionally related to 对教育有好处, so this is not a correction relationship for 不是……而是…….

examples.display: ⟦不是画画儿，而是祭拜⟧
examples.her_note: “不是……而是……” is used to refute something conventional and affirm something unexpected, and to correct something wrong, 画画儿 is not a conventional activity related to 寺庙
examples.explanation: 不是画画儿，而是祭拜: 画画儿 is not a conventional activity related to 寺庙, so 不是……而是…… does not fit here.

examples.display: 他[不是在→不再]搬家
examples.her_note: “不是……而是……” is used to refute something conventional and affirm something unexpected, and to correct something wrong, 搬家is not conventionally related to看文章
examples.explanation: 他不是在搬家 → 他不再搬家: 搬家 is not conventionally related to 看文章, so do not use 不是……而是…….

examples.display: [不是孟子喜欢这个城市，而是他喜欢这个城市的人→孟子不是喜欢这个城市，而是喜欢这个城市的人]
examples.original: 不是孟子喜欢这个城市，而是他喜欢这个城市的人
examples.corrected: 孟子不是喜欢这个城市，而是喜欢这个城市的人
examples.her_note: Subj. before “不是……而是……”
examples.explanation: 不是孟子喜欢这个城市，而是他喜欢这个城市的人 → 孟子不是喜欢这个城市，而是喜欢这个城市的人: put the subject 孟子 before 不是……而是…….

card.not_an_error: Do not flag a sentence that genuinely corrects a mistaken or conventional idea with an unexpected alternative. Do not use this pattern merely to connect two unrelated actions, places, or ideas.

name: 不是……就是……
definition: 不是……就是…… means “either…or…” and requires two genuinely alternative possibilities, not two compatible purposes, states, or actions.
her_notes: 不是……就是……is used for “either…or…”，here “学问” and “合适的地方” are actually the same purpose, to have a good environment for education
不是……就是……is used for “either…or…”, “高兴” and “安静” cannot form “either…or…” relationship

card.rule: Use 不是……就是…… for two real alternatives (“either…or…”). Put the Subj. at the beginning: <Subj.>不是……就是……; do not use it when the two parts are compatible or are the same purpose.
card.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: 不是……就是…… means “either…or…,” but <A> and <B> are not genuine alternative possibilities.

examples.display: 难怪孟子[不是高兴的孩子，就是安静的孩子→每天都不高兴]
examples.original: 不是高兴的孩子，就是安静的孩子
examples.her_note: 不是……就是……is used for “either…or…”, “高兴” and “安静” cannot form “either…or…” relationship
examples.explanation: 不是高兴的孩子，就是安静的孩子 → 每天都不高兴: “高兴” and “安静” cannot form an either…or… relationship.

examples.display: [不是学习中文，他就是跟老师说中文→他不是学习中文，就是跟老师说中文]
examples.original: 不是学习中文，他就是跟老师说中文
examples.corrected: 他不是学习中文，就是跟老师说中文
examples.her_note: Subj. at the beginning of 不是……就是……
examples.explanation: 不是学习中文，他就是跟老师说中文 → 他不是学习中文，就是跟老师说中文: put the subject at the beginning of 不是……就是…….

examples.display: [在孟母搬家的故事中，不是为了学问，就是为了以她搬家又搬着找合适的地方→孟母搬家是为了让孟子接受良好的教育]
examples.original: 在孟母搬家的故事中，不是为了学问，就是为了以她搬家又搬着找合适的地方
examples.corrected: 孟母搬家是为了让孟子接受良好的教育
examples.her_note: 不是……就是……is used for “either…or…”，here “学问” and “合适的地方” are actually the same purpose, to have a good environment for education
examples.explanation: 不是为了学问，就是为了以她搬家又搬着找合适的地方 → 孟母搬家是为了让孟子接受良好的教育: “学问” and “合适的地方” are the same purpose, not either…or….

examples.display: 从早到晚他[学习不是历史，就是哲学→不是学习历史，就是学习哲学]
examples.original: 学习不是历史，就是哲学
examples.corrected: 不是学习历史，就是学习哲学
examples.explanation: 学习不是历史，就是哲学 → 不是学习历史，就是学习哲学: use 不是……就是…… with the two alternative actions.

card.not_an_error: Do not flag 不是……就是…… when the two parts are genuinely alternative possibilities. With a shared subject, the subject can come before the connector.

name: 和 cannot connect clauses/verb phrases
definition: 和/跟 + noun connects multiple nouns that share the same action. Do not use it to connect whole clauses, unrelated verb phrases, adjectives, or an accompanying object that does not perform the action.
her_notes: “跟/和+noun.” is used for multiple nouns that have the same action, we can say: 马先生和张先生走……，because both 马先生and 张先生 “walk”, but here “驴” does not walk by itself, but walked by 马先生, so you need to use the accompanying phrase “V.着”

card.rule: 和/跟 + noun connects multiple nouns that share the same action. Do not use 和/跟 to connect clauses, verb phrases, or adjectives; if the noun is an accompanying object and does not do the action, use V.着 instead.
card.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: 和/跟 cannot connect <clauses/verb phrases/adjectives>. Use <correct connector or structure> instead.

examples.display: 孟子才四岁就开始学文学[-和]写汉字
examples.her_note: 和cannot connect verb phrases
examples.explanation: 学文学和写汉字 → 学文学，写汉字: 和 cannot connect verb phrases.

examples.display: 哲学人很聪明[和→也很]重要
examples.her_note: 和cannot connect Adj.
examples.explanation: 很聪明和重要 → 很聪明，也很重要: 和 cannot connect adjectives.

examples.display: 一个男生[和→牵着]一只驴从农人经过了
examples.her_note: “跟/和+noun.” is used for multiple nouns that have the same action, we can say: 一个男生和一个女生走……，because both 男生and 女生 “walk”, but here “驴” does not walk by itself, but walked by 男生, so you need to use the accompanying phrase “V.着”
examples.explanation: 一个男生和一只驴从农人经过了 → 一个男生牵着一只驴从农人经过了: 和 + noun is for nouns that share the same action; the donkey does not walk by itself, so use V.着.

examples.display: 但那些三个男孩不知不觉[和梨子→拿着梨子]走过了被偷走的有梨子所有权的第一个人
examples.her_note: “和+noun.” is used for multiple nouns that have the same action, we can say: 那三个男孩和拿走梨子的小男孩走过了……，because both 三个男孩 and 小男孩 “walk past…”, but here “梨子” do not walk, so you need to use the accompanying phrase “V.着”
examples.explanation: 和梨子走过了 → 拿着梨子走过了: 和 + noun is for nouns that share the same action; the pears do not walk, so use V.着.

card.not_an_error: 和/跟 + noun is correct when the nouns share the same action, such as 一个男生和一个女生走…… . Do not flag an accompanying noun when it is correctly expressed with V.着.

name: 比方说 / 特别是
definition: 比方说 introduces an example; delete it when no example follows. 特别是 + N, + clause singles out a typical example and must match the category being exemplified.
her_notes: 比方说is used to express “for example”, delete it
是不是有用了。比方说is used to express “for example”, delete it
”特别是+N, + Clause” is used to single out a typical example
特别是is used to single out a typical example, but夹竹桃is not an example of灵芝

card.rule: 比方说 introduces a following example; delete it when no example follows. 特别是+N, + Clause singles out a typical example, so N must be an example of the category.
card.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: <比方说> needs a following example, or <特别是+N, + Clause> must single out an N that is a typical example of <category>.

examples.display: [-比方说]
examples.her_note: 比方说is used to express “for example”, delete it
examples.explanation: 比方说 → delete: 比方说 means “for example,” but no example follows.

examples.display: ⟦特别是夹竹桃⟧对身体更不好
examples.her_note: 特别是is used to single out a typical example, but夹竹桃is not an example of灵芝
examples.explanation: 特别是夹竹桃: 特别是 should single out a typical example, but 夹竹桃 is not an example of 灵芝.

examples.display: 灵芝[特别是帮忙→特别有用]
examples.her_note: ”特别是+N, + Clause” is used to single out a typical example
examples.explanation: 灵芝特别是帮忙 → 灵芝特别有用: 特别是+N, + Clause is for singling out a typical example, not for describing 灵芝 as useful.

examples.display: 夹竹桃[是特别是毒→的毒特别厉害]
examples.her_note: ”特别是+N, + Clause” is used to single out a typical example
examples.explanation: 夹竹桃是特别是毒 → 夹竹桃的毒特别厉害: 特别是+N, + Clause is for singling out a typical example.

card.not_an_error: Do not flag 比方说 when it is followed by an actual example. Do not flag 特别是 when it has the 特别是+N, + Clause pattern and N is a typical example of the category.

name: loose connection / no logic relationship
definition: Make the relationship between clauses and sentences explicit. Add an appropriate connector, purpose, condition, place, or sequence marker when the narrative is fractured or loosely connected.
her_notes: loosely connected with the preceding sentence
no logic relationship with the preceding or following sentences
loose connection between the two clauses, 决定去旅行找到能吃的植物

card.rule: Make the relationship between clauses or sentences clear. Add or choose a connector, a purpose phrase, or a sequence marker that shows the real connection.
card.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: use <connector/purpose/sequence phrase> to show how this sentence connects to the previous clause or sentence.

examples.display: [+为了帮助人们找到能吃的植物，]神农旅行了
examples.corrected: 为了帮助人们找到能吃的植物，
examples.her_note: it is loosely connected with the previous sentence, better add “为了帮助人们找到能吃的植物”, 神农决定去旅行尝试新的植物，“过” is to express “experience”, now the experience has not yet been experienced
examples.explanation: 神农旅行了 → 为了帮助人们找到能吃的植物，神农旅行了: add a purpose phrase to connect his travel with its goal.

examples.display: [+接着]一下子就骑车逃跑
examples.her_note: otherwise it is broken from the preceding clause
examples.explanation: 一下子就骑车逃跑 → 接着一下子就骑车逃跑: add 接着 to show the next event in the sequence.

examples.display: [然后→因为]他认识他在山上吃的花
examples.explanation: 然后他认识他在山上吃的花 → 因为他认识他在山上吃的花: use 因为 to show the causal relationship, not sequence.

examples.display: 但我没想到[+的是]他可能很久以前并不是这样
examples.her_note: the coherence needs to be improved, 但我没想到的是
examples.explanation: 但我没想到他可能很久以前并不是这样 → 但我没想到的是他可能很久以前并不是这样: add 的是 to make the connection coherent.

name: condition is not definite
definition: Before expressions such as 这就要看……了, state an uncertain condition or alternative, for example 会不会生病 or 要不要吃.
her_notes: the component before “这就要看……了“ should be “not definite” condition, 他会不会生病
add a condition “会不会生病？” before “这就要看……了”
add a condition “要不要吃？” before “这就要看……了”

card.rule: Before 这就要看……了, state a not definite condition or alternative, such as 会不会生病, 要不要吃, or 蘑菇能不能吃.
card.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: Before 这就要看……了, add a not definite condition or alternative, such as <condition>.

examples.display: 他们[常常→会不会]生病了
examples.her_note: the condition is “not definite”
examples.explanation: 他们常常生病了 → 他们会不会生病: the condition is not definite.

examples.display: [+你要不要吃？]这就要看你饿不饿了
examples.her_note: add a condition “要不要吃？” before “这就要看……了”
examples.explanation: 这就要看你饿不饿了 → 你要不要吃？这就要看你饿不饿了: add the not definite condition 要不要吃？ before 这就要看……了.

examples.display: [+会不会生病？]这就要看什么植物吃了
examples.her_note: add a condition “会不会生病？” before “这就要看……了”
examples.explanation: 这就要看什么植物吃了 → 会不会生病？这就要看什么植物吃了: add the not definite condition 会不会生病？ before 这就要看……了.

examples.display: [+蘑菇能不能吃，]这就要看蘑菇看不看像伞
examples.her_note: e.g., 蘑菇能不能吃
examples.explanation: 这就要看蘑菇看不看像伞 → 蘑菇能不能吃，这就要看蘑菇看不看像伞: state the not definite condition 蘑菇能不能吃 before 这就要看……了.

examples.display: [+如果吃了夹竹桃，]这就要看你也吃不吃灵芝了
examples.her_note: e.g., 如果吃了夹竹桃
examples.explanation: 这就要看你也吃不吃灵芝了 → 如果吃了夹竹桃，这就要看你也吃不吃灵芝了: add the condition 如果吃了夹竹桃 before 这就要看……了.

name: wrong information
definition: Retell the traditional story accurately: do not add people, places, actions, objects, or character identities that are not in the story, and do not change established facts.
her_notes: wrong information, his father did not appear in this story
wrong information, 搬家因为孟母觉得it is not good to imitate how to buy and sell
wrong information, it’s not a temple but a school

card.rule: Use the story’s established facts when retelling it. Do not add or change people, places, actions, objects, identities, or causes; otherwise it is wrong information.
card.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: this changes a story fact; the story says <fact>.

examples.display: 可是⟦搬了十次家⟧
examples.her_note: wrong information, 搬了三次家
examples.explanation: 搬了十次家: this changes a story fact; the story says 搬了三次家.

examples.display: 所以他们最后搬到了⟦寺庙⟧
examples.her_note: wrong information, it’s not a temple but a school
examples.explanation: 寺庙: this changes a story fact; the final place is a school, not a temple.

examples.display: ⟦他爸爸说⟧
examples.her_note: wrong information, his father did not appear in this story
examples.explanation: 他爸爸说: this adds a person who is not in the story; his father did not appear.

examples.display: 孟子长大了以后⟦成为一名画家⟧
examples.her_note: wrong information, 哲学家
examples.explanation: 成为一名画家: this changes Mengzi’s identity; he became a 哲学家.

examples.display: ⟦夹竹桃很好吃，也对你的健康有好处⟧
examples.original: 夹竹桃很好吃，也对你的健康有好处
examples.her_note: wrong information, 夹竹桃 is a poison
examples.explanation: 夹竹桃很好吃，也对你的健康有好处: this changes a story fact; 夹竹桃 is a poison.

card.not_an_error: Do not flag a word or sentence under this rule only because of grammar or vocabulary. Flag it here when it changes or adds a fact in the traditional story.

name: miss information / result
definition: Include the important scene, action, motivation, or result needed for a complete retelling, rather than leaving a key event unexplained.
her_notes: miss information: 孟子 imitated how to offer sacrifices
it does not answer the previous Q “什么植物可以吃?”
wrong information, he directly ate夹竹桃

card.rule: Do not miss important information in a retelling: include the key scene, action, motivation, or result so the event is complete and clear.
card.explanation_template: <incomplete sentence> → <complete sentence>: add <missing information> to show <key action/result/scene>; this information is needed for the retelling.

examples.display: ⟦神农吃以后⟧
examples.her_note: miss the result of eating
examples.explanation: ⟦神农吃以后⟧: add the result of eating; the result is missing.

examples.display: ⟦孟母看出来孟子老是难过，害得他不能好好学习。⟧孟母恐怕孟子住在墓地的旁边对孟子有影响
examples.original: 孟母看出来孟子老是难过，害得他不能好好学习。
examples.her_note: miss information: 孟子 imitated how to offer sacrifices
examples.explanation: 孟母恐怕孟子住在墓地的旁边对孟子有影响: add that 孟子 imitated how to offer sacrifices; this important action is missing.

examples.display: 在当地的墓地找到了他跟别的孩子[+祭拜]
examples.explanation: 在当地的墓地找到了他跟别的孩子[+祭拜]: add 祭拜 to show what he and the other children did at the cemetery.

examples.display: [古代的时候住了孟子和孟母→在古代，孟子和孟母住在墓地边]
examples.original: 古代的时候住了孟子和孟母
examples.corrected: 在古代，孟子和孟母住在墓地边
examples.explanation: 古代的时候住了孟子和孟母 → 在古代，孟子和孟母住在墓地边: add the scene detail 墓地边 so the setting is clear.

card.not_an_error: Do not flag a sentence just because it does not include every possible detail. Flag it only when an important scene, action, motivation, or result is missing and the retelling is incomplete.

name: redundant
definition: Delete words, names, time phrases, or repeated structures that add no meaning or repeat information already expressed.
her_notes: “前途” itself means “hopeful future”, so “有希望” is a little bit redundant.

card.rule: Delete words, names, time phrases, or repeated structures when they add no new meaning or repeat information already given. For example, do not add 当 after 是, and do not use two words that express the same time or idea.
card.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: <deleted part> is redundant because <the remaining word(s)> already expresses this meaning.

examples.display: 他现在是[-当]医生
examples.her_note: redundant with是
examples.explanation: 是当医生 → 是医生: 当 is redundant with 是.

examples.display: 这个坏人好像没有什么⟦有希望的前途⟧
examples.her_note: “前途” itself means “hopeful future”, so “有希望” is a little bit redundant.
examples.explanation: 有希望的前途 → 前途: 有希望 is a little redundant because 前途 itself means a hopeful future.

examples.display: ⟦很久以前，在古代⟧有一个叫神农的老人
examples.her_note: “很久以前“ and ”在古代” are redundant, only keep one
examples.explanation: 很久以前，在古代 → keep only one: these two time phrases are redundant.

examples.display: 但那些三个男孩不知不觉和梨子走过了⟦被偷走的有梨子所有权的第一个人⟧
examples.original: 被偷走的有梨子所有权的第一个人
examples.her_note: “被偷走的有梨子所有权的第一个人” is too long, 第一个被偷走梨子的人 is clear enough.
examples.explanation: 被偷走的有梨子所有权的第一个人 → 第一个被偷走梨子的人: the longer repeated structure is unnecessary; the shorter phrase is clear enough.

card.not_an_error: Do not delete a word if it adds a different meaning, such as a different time, person, or detail. Only flag words or structures that repeat information already expressed.

name: add descriptive detail
definition: Use clear descriptive detail and internal-state language where needed so the retelling has sufficient scenes and is more expressive, not only a bare sequence of events.
her_notes: be specific, what不太好的事情？
一位很有名的文学家 -> 作家的家里

card.rule: Add specific descriptive detail, such as what kind, how much, or how often, when it makes the scene clearer and less like a bare sequence of events.
